titre: Christopher Nolan won't release The Odyssey deleted scenes because he doesn’t "believe in director's cuts"
chapo: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey is headed back to theaters

Christopher Nolan says there are plenty of deleted scenes from The Odyssey, but that we won't be seeing them anytime soon. "There’s a lot of deleted scenes scrumpled up in the wastebasket that no one will ever see," Nolan told The Independent. "I don’t really believe in director’s cuts. I want to stand by the film that goes out. As a writer-director, I try to do a lot of that weeding out. There aren’t many scenes that were shot." Continued Nolan: "On a film like this, to spend a day shooting something on top of a mountain or in the rain or on a boat or whatever that isn’t gonna be in the film, I would really rather not do that. And so I wanna stand behind the cuts of the films that are put out there.” The film hit theaters on July 17, stayed on premium large format screens until September 30, got another release in October, and will have one last IMAX 70mm release in December. It earned over $1.8 billion at the global box office, which officially makes it the highest-grossing R-rated movie of all time. The nearly three-hour-long movie was finally released on premium VOD, 4K, and DVD this week... and we're sad that there are no special deleted scenes included in the release. We can only imagine that a Nolan-style director's cut would put the film up to four, or even four-and-a-half hours, and yet I'd probably still go out to see that in 4DX. For more, check out our The Odyssey review, and our deep dives into The Odyssey monsters, The Odyssey poem, and The Odyssey ending explained. titre: Christopher Nolan Explains Why Fans Will Never See an Odyssey Director’s Cut
chapo: The Odyssey’s Christopher Nolan reveals why the epic’s home release has no director’s cut even if deleted scenes exist
extrait: Don’t expect to see any deleted scenes in the epic’s home release With a runtime of just under three hours, Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey doesn't necessarily need to be any longer, even as an adaptation of Homer's epic poem. Although it isn't Nolan's longest film, fans are always clamoring for more from the prolific director. With The Odyssey's release on home media​​​​​​​, there was some hope that a director's cut or deleted scenes would surface. Nolan has shut that idea down, going so far as to say people will likely never see director's cuts of his films. Nolan has been pretty excited about the home release of The Odyssey. While the director is known for shooting in IMAX and encouraging audiences to see his movies on the biggest screens possible, he also knows home viewing has a place in movie culture. Speaking to Polygon, Nolan said that at home the viewer is able to control the timeline and look at details, specifically saying that "it's really about the performances." He also supports talking over the movie​​​​​​​ in the comfort of your home. Still, home releases often come with bonuses such as deleted scenes. Nolan told The Independent, however, that isn't his style. “I don’t really believe in director’s cuts. I want to stand by the film that goes out,”​​​​​​​ the director said. He added that, in the case of The Odyssey, "there are a lot of deleted scenes up in the wastebasket that no one will ever see." Nolan stresses​​​​​​d that there aren't actually too many scenes that didn't make the final cut because shooting on film requires planning. "I tend to try and weed things out on paper because it’s crazy expensive to shoot things that aren’t going to be in the film." He admitted that this has led to a lack of bonuses on home releases, "which always disappoints the DVD crowd." For those watching the movie for the first time or the tenth time​​​​​​​, Nolan does have some opinions on how to best emulate the movie theater experience. Specifically, he suggests people get a projector. "You can get a relatively low-cost, pretty high-quality projector, darken your living room, maybe introduce some popcorn into the equation or whatever," he told Polygon. "Have a mini movie theater and do it on your own timeline. That's tremendous fun." Over the course of his career, Nolan said that he's been impressed by how much the home-viewing experience has improved thanks to technology like better projection technology​​​​​​​.
